root_cause.text: The MPTCP retransmission path holds `msk->fallback_lock` and then invokes `mptcp_sendmsg_frag`, which may call `__mptcp_try_fallback` that tries to acquire the same lock, causing a recursive locking deadlock.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check for `!msk->allow_subflows` in `__mptcp_retrans` to skip reinjection when an infinite fallback is in progress, preventing the recursive lock. The CVE description explicitly states the deadlock occurs because "the packet scheduler could attempt a reinjection after receiving an MP_FAIL and before the infinite map has been transmitted," and the lock trace shows `__mptcp_retrans` holding `fallback_lock` while `__mptcp_try_fallback` tries to acquire it again.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix MPTCP retransmission logic to skip retransmits when subflows are disallowed, even without a full fallback.
intent_record.what: Extended condition in __mptcp_retrans from only checking __mptcp_check_fallback(msk) to also checking !msk->allow_subflows, and updated associated comment to reflect that retransmission should be skipped when an infinite fallback is in progress (subflows disallowed).
intent_record.how: This change prevents the MPTCP retransmission path from executing when the socket has subflows disallowed (infinite fallback), causing the code to jump to the clear_scheduled label and skip retransmission in that scenario.
